transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We need to convene the quality-and-warehouse disposition huddle regarding the roof leak that exposed the 1,200 electric-motor housings in finished-goods storage overnight. We have four pallets -- P1, P2, P3, and P4, each with 300 units -- and the customer's Monday assembly schedule depends on these housings. Per our standard process, I'd like quality and warehouse each to state their current recorded findings so we can agree on a disposition and I can issue the formal decision.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good morning, Mara. Quality's current recorded finding is still being compiled -- I have an electrical laboratory report pending my sign-off covering the housings on pallets P2 and P4, but it has not yet been uploaded to the quality system. I'm not in a position to state a formal quality finding on those two pallets until that report is signed off and recorded. For pallets P1 and P3, I have no specific condition issue to report at this time. I'd like to hear what warehouse has recorded regarding which pallets were directly exposed before we proceed.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Warehouse's recorded finding is that P2 and P4 are the only pallets that received direct water exposure. The 600 units on those pallets correspond to Jon's tested lot, and the dry room can process them in exactly 6 hours before release, so P2 and P4 must remain segregated during drying. P1 and P3 are not identified as directly exposed.
